tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. It was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. (v2.3.1-rc was healthy only in staging, so it was not used.) After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened incident INC-0001 as a SEV2, which paged on-call.

- **Version chosen:** The broken release was v2.3.1, with about 18% of requests failing in us-east, us-west and eu-west. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. I skipped v2.3.1-rc because it was only ever healthy in staging, never in production.
- **Rollback:** All three regions now run v2.3.0, and health checks show the service as healthy with about 0.2% of requests failing.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the result. It also notes that the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before v2.3.1 is deployed again.

No approval was needed, because the policy only requires approval for deploying a version that has never been healthy in production.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0 (v2.3.1-rc was only healthy in staging).
